lijuan.1.tier_reason: Signature: the move most identified with Li Juan, and the easiest to tip into performed cuteness.
lijuan.1.why: Things we have stopped seeing are seen again, and the reader gets to be a stranger to them for a moment, which pulls attention back to detail. The narrator doesn't know, is curious, and reaches a childlike conclusion; the reader wants to laugh but is also moved by how seriously it is meant, and never feels lectured.
lijuan.1.example:
*Summary:* In *Winter Pasture* the author enters the winter camp as an outsider, and long stretches are about what she can't do, doesn't understand, and is curious about in life on the steppe.

*Demo:* I always assumed the escalator at the subway station ran all the time. Then one morning I got there too early and saw it standing still, like a long sleeping worm, and realized it had a shift to clock in for too.
lijuan.1.breakdown:
- "I always assumed": put the silly belief on the table first; admit you didn't know.
- "got there too early": one concrete occasion breaks the misunderstanding.
- "it had a shift to clock in for": the conclusion is a child's, not a science lesson.
lijuan.1.overdo:
> Wow, so escalators need their beauty sleep too, sooo cute! It made me realize that everything needs rest, and we should learn to be kind to ourselves.

The trouble: playing cute, then immediately bolting on a grown-up moral.
lijuan.1.when_not:
- On a subject you actually know well, pretending not to is a performance.
- In serious events (illness, accidents), naivety reads as flippant.
lijuan.1.exercise: Write about an everyday thing you misunderstood for a long time as a child, in two sentences built on "I always thought… until…". No commentary.
lijuan.1.check: The conclusion is childlike, and there is no "so it turns out" or "it made me realize" moral patched on.
lijuan.1.adjacent: lijuan.4 Self-Mockery is about being clumsy; Naive Eye is about never having seen it before. In wangzengqi.2 the "I" is a knowledgeable insider, the exact opposite.

lijuan.2.tier_reason: Core: the base layer of nearly every Li Juan piece; without it the other moves have nothing to stand on.
lijuan.2.why: A summary lets the reader skip; filling it in puts the reader in the room. Honest numbers and one absurd little detail give an ordinary task weight and a sense of truth. What readers remember is often the least remarkable number.
lijuan.2.example:
*Summary:* The chapters of *My Altay* on the family's small shop, the tailoring work and housework often follow one job from start to finish.

*Demo:* When we made dumplings, I rolled the wrappers. I rolled one, Mom filled one; when she finished she had to wait for me, so she tapped the rim of the bowl with her chopsticks. I rolled forty-six in all, nine of them oval.
lijuan.2.breakdown:
- "I rolled one, Mom filled one": the rhythm follows the back-and-forth of the action.
- "tapped the rim of the bowl": waiting is written as an action, not as "she got impatient".
- "forty-six, nine oval": a number precise to the point of absurdity leaves something to remember.
lijuan.2.overdo:
> First we made the dough, then the filling, then rolled the wrappers, and finally filled, boiled and served the dumplings. The whole family was happy together and spent a warm evening.

The trouble: every step is there but all of it is summary, with no detail to remember, and "warm" is stuck on at the end.
lijuan.2.when_not:
- When the piece needs to move fast, filling in drags.
- If everything in a piece is filled in, readers tire; pick the one thing most worth it.
lijuan.2.exercise: Record one chore you did today. Write at least three steps and two exact numbers, one of them needlessly exact.
lijuan.2.check: The paragraph has one concrete number or detail that makes you want to laugh or remember it, and no "warm" or "happy together".
lijuan.2.adjacent: wangzengqi.3 writes other people's craft in detail, with respect; in lijuan.6 Earnest Exaggeration the numbers are deliberately inflated, while here they are real.

lijuan.3.tier_reason: Core: how Li Juan handles any landscape, and a basic skill any descriptive writing can use.
lijuan.3.why: Big words tell the reader that something is beautiful; plain sketching lets them see it. One exact shape or trace lights the picture up better than "a world clad in silver", and it is more believable, because only someone who was there could have seen it.
lijuan.3.example:
*Summary:* The passages in *Corners of Altay* on wilderness, rivers and the turn of seasons rest on concrete visible things, with few lyrical adjectives.

*Demo:* It snowed all night. In the morning every car downstairs had gone white, except for one with a small patch wiped clear on the windshield, round, probably by someone's sleeve.
lijuan.3.breakdown:
- "every car had gone white": one word, "white", gives the whole view, unadorned.
- "a small patch wiped clear", "round": find one exception inside the whole view.
- "someone's sleeve": from the object to a person, and the scene has someone in it.
lijuan.3.overdo:
> Overnight the land was wrapped in silver, beautiful beyond words; pure white snowflakes covered every corner of the city, like a magnificent painting.

The trouble: stock four-character phrases and big words piled up like a tourism brochure, with nothing that belongs only to this snowfall.
lijuan.3.when_not:
- When the scenery is just a passing backdrop, don't sketch it closely.
- For a scene you haven't really looked at, you can't produce the exception; don't make one up.
lijuan.3.exercise: Open the window and write what's in front of you in three sentences: one for the whole view, one for an exception, one leading from that detail to a person. No set phrases.
lijuan.3.check: No more than two adjectives in the paragraph, and one concrete detail that no other snow, rain or wind would have.
lijuan.3.adjacent: wangzengqi.7 names single plants and their uses; lijuan.8 Pull Back is a change of scale, while Landscape Sketch gets the near things exact.

lijuan.4.tier_reason: Common: works in any personal essay, but it needs a real, specific mishap behind it.
lijuan.4.why: When the narrator lowers herself first, the reader stands beside her instead of in the audience. Laughter closes the distance, and the reader is more willing to believe everything else this not-so-clever person says; it also keeps any sadness later from seeming affected.
lijuan.4.example:
*Summary:* Across her collections the author often writes about being clumsy at work, being despaired of by her family, and looking foolish in unfamiliar places.

*Demo:* I've been learning to swim for three years and still know only one stroke. My coach calls it "the distress signal".
lijuan.4.breakdown:
- "three years", "only one": numbers make the clumsiness concrete.
- "My coach calls it": the verdict comes from someone else; she doesn't explain.
- "the distress signal": the laugh lands on the last words, with nothing added.
lijuan.4.overdo:
> I'm seriously such an idiot, I can't do anything right, hahaha. But even though I'm dumb, I'm sincere, and that's kind of cute, right?

The trouble: empty self-putdown followed straight away by self-praise, without one concrete mishap.
lijuan.4.when_not:
- In formal documents or job applications.
- When the self-mockery touches real illness or trauma, readers can't laugh.
lijuan.4.exercise: Write about a small thing you botched recently, using one number and one remark from someone else. Under 50 words.
lijuan.4.check: The laugh comes from concrete facts and other people's words, not from labels like "I'm so dumb".
lijuan.4.adjacent: lijuan.1 Naive Eye is never having seen it; Self-Mockery is not being able to do it. luxun.8 Self-Dissection is a serious cut into oneself; this is a light-hearted mishap.

lijuan.5.tier_reason: Signature: the mother and grandmother are the best-known figures in her books, and the line between fondness and mockery is fine.
lijuan.5.why: The reader watches a real person do something earnest and funny, and the laugh happens on its own. Because the author doesn't judge, the care inside the clumsiness is seen too, and the comedy and the ache arrive together.
lijuan.5.example:
*Summary:* In *My Altay* and *The Distant Sunflower Fields*, the mother and grandmother recur, often creating comedy through what they plainly say and do.

*Demo:* The first time Mom tried voice input, she shouted at her phone one word at a time: "I. Am. At. The. Supermarket." Then, not trusting it, she held the phone up to her ear, as if she could hear whether it had remembered.
lijuan.5.breakdown:
- "one word at a time": the breaks put her seriousness straight into the dialogue.
- "held the phone up to her ear": one action does more than calling her "bad with technology".
- "as if she could hear whether it had remembered": only a guess, not ridicule.
lijuan.5.overdo:
> My mother is a hardworking, simple countrywoman. She didn't have much schooling, but she loves us quietly in her own way. She is the best mother in the world.

The trouble: summary praise; the person never moves, and nothing is funny.
lijuan.5.when_not:
- Private matters family members don't want written, or things that would embarrass real relatives.
- Mourning, illness and similar situations, where a comic touch hurts.
lijuan.5.exercise: Write one line a family member actually said and one action, while they were trying something new. No words describing their character.
lijuan.5.check: Readers can laugh, but afterwards don't feel the family member was mocked; no "hardworking", "simple", "the best".
lijuan.5.adjacent: wangzengqi.4 sketches outsiders to make them stand up, not to get a laugh; in lijuan.4 Self-Mockery the joke is on "me", here it's on the family.

lijuan.6.tier_reason: Common: usable in any light essay, provided the tone stays straight.
lijuan.6.why: The more serious the tone, the funnier the exaggeration. The reader goes back and forth once between "that's impossible" and "but it kind of is", and that is where the laugh comes from. An outlandish comparison, because it fits so closely, can be more accurate than plain description.
lijuan.6.example:
*Summary:* Pieces such as those in *Corners of Altay* often describe everyday things through earnest counting and unexpected comparisons.

*Demo:* The cat downstairs is fat in a very opinionated way. It never looks at the cars when it crosses the road. The cars look at it.
lijuan.6.breakdown:
- "fat in a very opinionated way": body and personality forced together, absurd but said straight.
- "never looks at the cars… the cars look at it": subject and object swap; the syntax does the exaggerating.
- Not a single exclamation in it; no breaking character.
lijuan.6.overdo:
> The cat downstairs is so fat I'm literally dead, it's insane, the ground shakes when it walks, who could see it and not say legend!

The trouble: internet-joke voice; "literally dead" and "insane" laugh for the reader, and the honesty is gone.
lijuan.6.when_not:
- In passages that need accurate information (times, prices, facts), exaggeration misleads.
- Where other people's flaws (looks, disability) are involved, it easily becomes mockery.
lijuan.6.exercise: Pick something near you (an old computer, worn slippers) and exaggerate one of its traits in one serious sentence, with no internet slang.
lijuan.6.check: Ignore the content and listen only to the tone: it sounds like a statement of fact. No "literally", "insane", "totally".
lijuan.6.adjacent: wangxiaobo.1 is a chain of deadpan reasoning; this is a single exaggerated line. In lijuan.2 Chores in Full the numbers are real; here they are inflated.

lijuan.7.tier_reason: Common: fits any writing about animals, plants or weather, as long as it stays out of fairy tale.
lijuan.7.why: Once things have tempers, the world gets lively. "I" earnestly talking to a pot of grass that ignores me is funny in its one-sided seriousness, and it also lets the narrator's loneliness and tenderness show through.
lijuan.7.example:
*Summary:* In passages about dogs, sheep, plants and small animals, the author often guesses at what they are thinking and talks to them.

*Demo:* The pothos on the balcony is nearly dead for the third time. When I water it I say, "Hang in there a bit longer." It ignores me and yellows another leaf.
lijuan.7.breakdown:
- "nearly dead for the third time": a number gives the plant a medical history.
- "Hang in there a bit longer": talking to a plant as to a person, quite seriously.
- "It ignores me": personified but not a fairy tale; it goes on yellowing.
lijuan.7.overdo:
> Hearing my encouragement, the little pothos happily waved its leaves, as if smiling at me: "Thank you, I'll do my best to grow!"

The trouble: personification turned fairy tale, the plant playing along, sugary and false.
lijuan.7.when_not:
- In popular science or explanatory writing, personification gets in the way of facts.
- If you want to use an animal to preach a big lesson, better not to use it at all.
lijuan.7.exercise: Say one sentence to something at home (a plant, the fridge, the cat), then write how it "responds" — only in ways it really could.
lijuan.7.check: The personified thing's reaction is entirely possible in reality; it doesn't "smile" or "speak".
lijuan.7.adjacent: wangzengqi.7 does not personify, only names plants and their uses; mao.4 uses folk comparisons for argument.

lijuan.8.tier_reason: Signature: a distinctive move that only works once per piece and only after the close-up work is done.
lijuan.8.why: The closer and finer the writing before it, the bigger the drop when the view widens. The reader suddenly sees the person they cared about swallowed by the crowd or the land, small and earnest, and the feeling arrives without being said. Used only once, it carries weight.
lijuan.8.example:
*Summary:* *Winter Pasture* writes about scattered households and flocks in the wilderness; the smallness of people in vast space is the book's ground tone.

*Demo:* From the nineteenth floor, the crowd of people leaving work stops at the crossing, then scatters when the light turns green. My mom is down there somewhere, carrying a bag of scallions. I can't tell which one she is.
lijuan.8.breakdown:
- "From the nineteenth floor": a vantage point, so the pull-back has grounds.
- "stops… scatters": write the movement of the crowd, not a reflection on it.
- "a bag of scallions", "can't tell which one": inside the large there is still one specific small thing, and the feeling lands on "can't tell".
lijuan.8.overdo:
> Standing up high, I suddenly felt how tiny humanity is; before the vast universe, our worries are not worth mentioning.

The trouble: after pulling back it goes straight to a lesson, with no picture and no small person.
lijuan.8.when_not:
- If the piece has already pulled back once, a second time has no weight.
- If the piece hasn't yet written anything close and detailed, there is no drop.
lijuan.8.exercise: First write one close-up action of a family member, then one sentence seeing the same person from high up or far away.
lijuan.8.check: The pulled-back passage contains a specific person and object, and no "tiny", "universe", "not worth mentioning".
lijuan.8.adjacent: wangzengqi.5 shifts sideways to another place or year; zhexuan.6 raises the conceptual level, while this is a change of visual scale.

lijuan.9.tier_reason: Core: her basic way of handling feeling, and the restraint every other move depends on.
lijuan.9.why: The reader has been moving through chores, is suddenly struck by one sentence, and is pulled back to the stove before having time to brace. The feeling isn't diluted, so the aftershock lasts longer. Restraint makes the reader believe the feeling is real.
lijuan.9.example:
*Summary:* At tender or sad moments the pieces often pass with one short sentence and move straight on to the next small thing.

*Demo:* It suddenly occurred to me that she counted me year by year the way she was counting these peppers one by one. Then the oil in the pan crackled, and she called me to turn off the heat.
lijuan.9.breakdown:
- "It suddenly occurred to me": the feeling arrives abruptly, without setup.
- "one by one… year by year": even the sigh rests on the action in front of her.
- "the oil in the pan crackled": straight back to the chores; the feeling gets no second sentence.
lijuan.9.overdo:
> At that moment I finally understood the greatness of a mother's love. So she had been giving all along, so the years had already crept onto her temples, so… my tears poured out.

The trouble: sigh after sigh, "finally understood" and "so" stacked up, the feeling talked out.
lijuan.9.when_not:
- If the piece doesn't yet have enough chores underneath, the sigh feels abrupt.
- In forms that need full expression of feeling (eulogies, love letters), one sentence may not be enough.
lijuan.9.exercise: In the middle of a paragraph about housework, insert one reflection of no more than 25 words; the next sentence must immediately be a sound or an action.
lijuan.9.check: No more than two reflective sentences in the piece, each followed right away by a concrete action or sound.
lijuan.9.adjacent: lijuan.10 Stop on an Action is an ending, while One Light Sigh turns mid-piece; sushi.6 pauses to turn toward a principle, but this offers no principle.

lijuan.10.tier_reason: Core: how nearly every Li Juan piece ends, and an ending any personal essay can borrow.
lijuan.10.why: The last action is left for the reader to interpret, so the aftertaste is the reader's own. A slightly funny action keeps the ending light but resonant, and more memorable than a lesson.
lijuan.10.example:
*Summary:* Many of the essays end on an everyday action or scene, with no summing up.

*Demo:* I said there was no room left on the balcony. She looked at my treadmill and said nothing.
lijuan.10.breakdown:
- "I said… no room left": a small conflict is thrown out.
- "looked at my treadmill": her plan is hidden in the action, not spelled out.
- "said nothing": it stops on silence, leaving the laugh and the aftertaste to the reader.
lijuan.10.overdo:
> Looking at the balcony full of green, I thought, this must be life at its most beautiful. May we all be like Mom and grow our own hope in the ordinary.

The trouble: a feel-good ending with "this is life" and "may we all", finishing the thought for the reader.
lijuan.10.when_not:
- Explanatory writing or reports that need a clear conclusion.
- If the conflict earlier hasn't been made clear, stopping on an action leaves readers lost.
lijuan.10.exercise: Rewrite the ending of a short piece about a family member: cut the closing reflection and replace it with something they did or said.
lijuan.10.check: The last paragraph could be drawn as a single picture, and contains no "life", "understood", "may".
lijuan.10.adjacent: wangzengqi.10 is almost the same structure, but Wang Zengqi is gentler and doesn't aim for a laugh; luxun.10 Unresolved Ending carries a cold, hanging question.
